clue.text: French writer quietly enters university territory

indicators.note: the quiet letter goes inside the writer's name, as the clue says it enters

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A French author quietly slips onto a university's grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings belonging to a university or college.

clue.text: Profit made with this, say, in West London?

annotationWithheld.why: Profit made with this, say, in West London? (5): AVAIL means profit, but no parse of 'made with this, say, in West London' gives or confirms the letters; possibly an OCR garble or a pun not recoverable.
annotationWithheld.clue: Profit made with this, say, in West London?

clue.text: Having foreknowledge, set out round islands

indicators.note: the verb phrase goes round the islands, so its letters enclose them

parts.note: to set out goods is to present them
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Someone with foresight sets out on a tour of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym for PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescient describes someone who knows of events before they happen.

clue.text: Passionate Eastern ruler loses article on railway

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next
the ruler's title loses the article, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a sultan is a ruler in Muslim countries of the East
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ardent Eastern potentate gives up an item to travel by train.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultry can mean sensual or passionate, as well as hot and humid.

clue.text: Russian secret police chief involved in wrongdoing

indicators.note: the police chief is wrapped up inside the wrongdoing, so one sits within the other

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD

explanation.surface: A Soviet secret police boss is implicated in some misdeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siberian comes from Siberia, so is Russian, as an example of the broader class.

clue.text: Broadcast inappropriately, indulging youthful excess

definitions.meaning: literally, to scatter seed of a useless weedy grass where it does not belong
the idiom for a young person's period of wild behaviour

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a youthful spell of promiscuity or excess, from scattering worthless wild grass seed.

clue.text: Claret, for instance, or port

definitions.meaning: claret is red wine of the ... region, an example of such wine
A port city on the Garonne in France

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both the wine from that region and the French seaport city itself.

clue.text: Old widow has no time for surviving custom

indicators.note: the widow word lacks the time letter, so it is removed

parts.note: relict is an archaic word for a widow

explanation.surface: An elderly widow has no time for traditions that linger.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic can be a custom or belief surviving from an earlier era.

clue.text: Lancaster ruin inherited from forebears

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, signalling the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruined castle at Lancaster was passed down through the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' looks like a noun for a castle, but it signals rearranging LANCASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral means belonging to or handed down from one's ancestors.

clue.text: Robber's secure means of communication

parts.note: safe means secure
blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A thief has a reliable way of getting messages through.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A safeblower is a criminal who blows open safes with explosives, a kind of robber.

clue.text: Hold a tuft of wool

definitions.meaning: a small bunch of hair or wool

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a grip that immobilises an opponent and a small bunch of fibres.

clue.text: Choose man to identify subatomic particle

parts.note: to elect is to choose
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: Pick a man to name a particular particle.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is a negatively charged subatomic particle.

clue.text: Pardon former copper beginning to sell illegal drug

parts.note: ex means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: only the start of the next word is taken, its opening letter

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, an illegal drug

explanation.surface: A retired policeman starting to deal drugs seeks forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to pardon or forgive them.

clue.text: Dogs, for example, or man with capital?

definitions.meaning: the ... of Dogs is a district of east London

explanation.definitionFit: Both names, Dogs and Man, follow the word for an island in a place name.

clue.text: Disorganised mob has loony left in charge

indicators.note: loony means crazy, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chaotic crowd is led by a mad leftist.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is British informal for chaotic and disorganised.

clue.text: Small kitchen vessel used by youth leader

indicators.note: the boat word is used alongside the next piece, placed just before it

parts.note: a sculler is a small rowing boat propelled by sculls

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small kitchen pot is wielded by the head of a youth club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small kitchen vessel' reads as a pan, but 'vessel' is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery is a small room off a kitchen for washing dishes.

clue.text: Parodist makes light, at first, of heavy blow

parts.note: a lamp is a light

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: oner is British slang for a heavy blow

explanation.surface: A satirist provides illumination before a knockout punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampooner ridicules people through satire, which is what a parodist does.

clue.text: Quick snack? This course is for trainees

definitions.meaning: a ... course in Britain alternates college study with periods of work training

explanation.definitionFit: A snack of filling between bread, and a British course mixing study with work placements.

clue.text: Meat dish I put on father's vehicle

indicators.note: in this across clue the I is put on after the vehicle

parts.note: pa is father, so pa's is father's
a tram is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone places themselves on Dad's tram with a dish of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned smoked beef, often served as a deli dish.

clue.text: Scottish island's non-acidic humus

definitions.meaning: An island in the Inner Hebrides
a soil scientist's term for humus formed in non-acid conditions

explanation.definitionFit: The name of a Hebridean island and a technical term for crumbly, non-acid forest soil humus.

clue.text: Idiot warily observes sound Scottish jury

parts.note: an ass is an idiot

indicators.note: the word is taken as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: to eye someone is to watch them warily, so eyes means warily observes

explanation.surface: A fool keeps a cautious watch on a Scottish jury.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law an assize was a jury, as well as the historic court sessions in England.

clue.text: A Bronx woman overseas

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman, so a New Yorker from the Bronx might say it

explanation.surface: A woman from the Bronx is now living in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in or to a foreign country, overseas.

clue.text: Possibly stomach a specialist magazine

definitions.meaning: the stomach is an example of a bodily ...
a periodical serving a particular group or cause

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a body part such as the stomach and a publication of a society or interest group.

clue.text: Come upon fellow turning back bedspread

indicators.note: the name is turned round, read from right to left

parts.note: Sid is a man's name, a fellow
a cover is a bedspread

explanation.surface: Stumble on a man pulling back the bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses SID to give DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to come upon or find something.

clue.text: Gray's distant prospect, say, having taken courses?

indicators.note: say asks us to take the school's name as spoken

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote 'Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College', so the distant prospect is the school

explanation.surface: A poet's view of a far landscape belongs to someone who has done their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests study, as at a school, but means meal courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has taken the courses of a meal has eaten them, a playful sense.

clue.text: Boxer receives pound for publicity

indicators.note: the boxer takes in the pound letter, holding it inside

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A prizefighter is paid a pound to promote something.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a piece of free publicity for a product or event.

clue.text: Single climber entering gallery of national character

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single

indicators.note: the climbing plant goes inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
a liana is a tropical climbing plant

explanation.surface: A lone mountaineer walks into a gallery with a distinctly national air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer but is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Italianate means having Italian style or character, the character of one nation.

clue.text: A container accordingly provided for a prickly plant

parts.note: a can is a container
thus means accordingly

explanation.surface: A tin is therefore supplied for a spiky shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a genus of plants with spiny, prickly leaves.

clue.text: Going astray, arrives back in hospital department

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: A wandering patient turns up back at an ear, nose and throat ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course, wandering.
